_schema.note: Each category's 'resources' array holds objects with this shape. Filling the directory is just adding objects here — no other file needs to change.

resource.name: string — resource name
resource.type: string — one of: website, tool, guide, dataset, organization, publication

resources.name: Consumer Federation of America
resources.description: A nonprofit association of consumer groups that has advocated for US consumers since 1968. Publishes research, tips and policy analysis on banking fees, credit, debt collection and financial products.

resources.name: National Consumer Law Center
resources.description: Nonprofit consumer law experts working on behalf of low-income consumers. Their free consumer-facing resources explain debt collection, credit reporting, student loans and what to do when a lender breaks the rules.

resources.name: National Foundation for Credit Counseling (NFCC)
resources.description: The largest US network of nonprofit credit counseling agencies. Its agency finder connects people with accredited counselors for budgeting and debt management plans, as an alternative to for-profit debt relief companies.

resources.name: r/personalfinance Wiki
resources.description: Community-maintained wiki from one of the largest personal finance forums online. Known for its step-by-step 'what to do with my money' flowchart, plus plain guides on debt, banking and building credit.

resources.name: StepChange Debt Charity
resources.description: UK charity offering free, confidential debt advice online and by phone, including an online debt tool that builds a personal action plan and debt solutions without fees.

resources.name: Which? Money
resources.description: The money section of Which?, the UK's consumer association. Independent guides on bank accounts, savings, credit and scams, with practical advice on complaining and getting money back.

resources.name: Better Finance
resources.description: The European federation of investors and financial services users. Independent research and campaigns on banking fees, retail investment products and pensions from the consumer side.

resources.name: Financial Rights Legal Centre
resources.description: Australian community legal centre that helps people with debt, credit, banking and insurance problems. Free fact sheets, sample letters and a national helpline.

resources.name: United Policyholders
resources.description: Nonprofit that helps policyholders navigate insurance claims, especially after disasters. Free claim guides, sample letters, a 'Roadmap to Recovery' program and practical tips for resolving disputes with insurers.

resources.name: Consumer Watchdog
resources.description: California-based nonprofit consumer group with a long track record on insurance rates and practices. Publishes investigations, consumer alerts and case updates on insurer conduct.

resources.name: Citizens Advice – Insurance
resources.description: Free, step-by-step guidance from the UK charity on what to do when an insurer refuses or delays a claim, how to complain, and when to escalate to the Financial Ombudsman.

resources.name: Resolver
resources.description: Free online tool that helps you raise and track complaints with insurers and other companies, keeps all correspondence in one place and guides you through escalation if the company doesn't respond.

resources.name: Fairer Finance
resources.description: Independent UK consumer group that rates insurers and banks on customer experience and policy quality, and publishes a regular Trust in Insurance Index. Useful for comparing how insurers actually treat customers.

resources.name: CHOICE – Insurance advice
resources.description: Guides from Australia's leading independent consumer organisation on choosing insurance, understanding exclusions and what to do when a claim goes wrong.

resources.name: Consumer Action Law Centre
resources.description: Australian community legal centre with free fact sheets and toolkits on insurance disputes, unfair claims handling and consumer rights, plus a free legal advice line for Victorians.

resources.name: Web3 is Going Just Great
resources.description: An independent, sourced timeline of crypto scams, hacks, rug pulls and collapses, with a running total of losses. A sober reality check before putting money into any crypto project.

resources.name: Citation Needed
resources.description: Independent newsletter and podcast by Molly White, the researcher behind Web3 is Going Just Great. Clear, well-sourced analysis of crypto, fintech and the policies around them, written for non-specialists.

resources.name: Chainabuse
resources.description: Free community database of reported crypto scams. Search a wallet address, website or domain to see if others have reported it, or file your own report to warn people.

resources.name: Revoke.cash
resources.description: Free, open-source tool to see and cancel the token approvals your crypto wallet has granted. Its learning section explains in plain language how approval scams drain wallets and how to protect yourself.

resources.name: Global Anti-Scam Organization (GASO)
resources.description: Volunteer-run nonprofit founded by scam survivors. Supports victims of romance and crypto investment scams ('pig butchering'), publishes scam reports and warns about fake 'fund recovery' services.

resources.name: Operation Shamrock
resources.description: Nonprofit coalition fighting pig-butchering and crypto investment scams. Its library and podcast explain how these scams work, who runs them and what victims can do.

resources.name: AARP – Cryptocurrency Scams
resources.description: Plain-language guide from AARP's Fraud Watch Network on how crypto scams work, including crypto ATM and romance scams, and the warning signs to share with older relatives.

resources.name: NCLC – Payments & Payment Fraud
resources.description: Resources from the National Consumer Law Center on payment apps like Zelle and Cash App, prepaid cards and fintech accounts. Explains which protections you have when money is stolen or sent to a scammer.

resources.name: LawHelp.org
resources.description: Run by the nonprofit Pro Bono Net, it connects people with free legal aid organizations in their state and offers plain-language guides on consumer, housing, debt and family law problems.

resources.name: Wex – Legal Information Institute (Cornell)
resources.description: Free, collaborative legal dictionary and encyclopedia from Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute. Clear definitions of contract and consumer-law terms you'll meet in agreements and disputes.

resources.name: Terms of Service; Didn't Read
resources.description: Community project that reads and grades the terms of service and privacy policies of popular websites and apps, highlighting the clauses that matter. Also available as a browser extension.

resources.name: Upsolve
resources.description: Nonprofit that offers a free online tool to file Chapter 7 bankruptcy without a lawyer for people who qualify, plus a large library of plain-English guides on debt, collections and lawsuits.

resources.name: CourtListener
resources.description: Free, nonprofit legal search engine from the Free Law Project. Search millions of court opinions and federal court records, and set alerts on cases you're following.

resources.name: Which? Consumer Rights – Template Letters
resources.description: Free template letters from the UK consumer association for complaints, refunds, faulty goods, cancelled contracts and compensation claims, each with guidance on your legal rights.

resources.name: Advicenow
resources.description: Run by the charity Law for Life, it publishes independent, practical guides to help people in England and Wales understand and deal with legal problems on their own, from disputes to tribunals.

resources.name: LawWorks
resources.description: Charity that connects people who can't afford a lawyer with free legal advice clinics across England and Wales, staffed by volunteer lawyers.

resources.name: Justice Connect
resources.description: Australian not-for-profit providing free legal help and plain-language self-help resources, including support for people facing debt, bankruptcy and unfair contracts.

resources.name: JustFix
resources.description: Nonprofit building free tools for tenants: send repair request letters to landlords, research who really owns a building, and understand your rights. Strongest for New York, with guidance useful far beyond it.

resources.name: National Low Income Housing Coalition
resources.description: Nonprofit research and advocacy group focused on affordable housing for renters. Publishes the annual 'Out of Reach' report on what it costs to rent in every US state and tracks renter protections.

resources.name: National Housing Law Project
resources.description: Nonprofit housing law organization with a free resource center on tenant rights, evictions and subsidized housing, plus know-your-rights material for renters and the people who help them.

resources.name: Shelter
resources.description: UK housing charity with detailed, free advice on private renting: deposits, repairs, rent increases, evictions and getting help with rent. Also runs a free housing advice helpline.

resources.name: Tenants' Union of NSW
resources.description: Community legal centre and peak body for renters in New South Wales. Clear factsheets on leases, bonds, repairs, rent increases and ending a tenancy, including Easy Read versions.

resources.name: Tenants Victoria
resources.description: Not-for-profit community legal centre for renters in Victoria, with free advice and plain-language guides on renting rights, repairs, bonds and evictions.

resources.name: ACORN Canada
resources.description: Independent tenant and community union organizing renters across Canada, with campaigns and resources on rent increases, repairs and renovictions.

resources.name: Consumers' Checkbook
resources.description: Nonprofit consumer organization that rates local contractors and home service providers based on customer surveys and price comparisons, with no advertising from the companies it rates.

resources.name: Rebuilding Together
resources.description: National nonprofit network providing free critical home repairs and accessibility modifications for low-income homeowners, older adults and veterans through local affiliates.

resources.name: Rewiring America
resources.description: Nonprofit focused on home electrification. Free calculators and guides to find rebates and tax credits for heat pumps, insulation, induction stoves and solar, and estimate real savings.

resources.name: iFixit
resources.description: Free, community-written repair guides for appliances, electronics and household items. A good first stop before paying for a repair or replacing something that might be easy to fix.

resources.name: Energy Saving Trust
resources.description: Independent UK organisation with impartial advice on insulation, heating, heat pumps and solar panels, including what to check before hiring an installer.

resources.name: Which? Trusted Traders
resources.description: Directory of UK tradespeople who have passed checks by the consumer association Which?, including references, credit checks and an assessment of how they work. Traders pay to join after vetting.

resources.name: Repair Café
resources.description: International volunteer movement of free repair meetups where people bring broken household items and fix them with volunteers. Find a Repair Café near you on the world map.

resources.name: Renew
resources.description: Australian not-for-profit helping households make their homes more comfortable and energy-efficient, with independent guides on solar, batteries, heating, cooling and renovations.
Free, confidential service supported by United Way that connects people with local help for bills, food, housing, utilities and more, by phone, text or online.

resources.name: Turn2us
resources.description: UK charity with a free benefits calculator and grants search to check what financial support you may be entitled to, plus guides on claiming and challenging benefit decisions.

resources.name: Ask Izzy
resources.description: Free, anonymous Australian directory built by the not-for-profit Infoxchange to find nearby services for housing, food, money help, health and legal support.

resources.name: Citizens Advice – Benefits
resources.description: Independent charity guidance on UK benefits: checking eligibility, applying, and challenging decisions through mandatory reconsideration and appeals.

resources.name: Workplace Fairness
resources.description: Nonprofit with free, plain-language information on US employment law: wages and overtime, discrimination, harassment, leave, firing and workplace injuries, organized by topic and state.

resources.name: A Better Balance
resources.description: Nonprofit legal organization with free know-your-rights guides and a helpline for workers on pregnancy, family leave, sick time and caregiving rights at work.

resources.name: JobWatch
resources.description: Australian employment law community legal centre offering free, confidential advice and factsheets on unfair dismissal, underpayment, bullying and discrimination at work.

resources.name: FlyersRights
resources.description: The largest US nonprofit airline passenger organization. Explains your rights on delays, cancellations, refunds and tarmac waits, and campaigns for stronger passenger protections.

resources.name: Elliott Report
resources.description: Consumer advocacy site by journalist Christopher Elliott that helps travelers resolve disputes with airlines, hotels and car rental companies, with guides on how to fix your own consumer problem.

resources.name: Wikivoyage
resources.description: Free, community-written travel guide from the Wikimedia movement, with practical, ad-free information on destinations, getting around, costs and staying safe.

resources.name: The Man in Seat 61
resources.description: Independent, award-winning guide to train travel in Europe and worldwide: routes, how to book, real fares and tips to avoid overpaying through third-party sites.

resources.name: Khan Academy
resources.description: Nonprofit offering free, world-class courses in maths, science, economics and personal finance for learners of any age.

resources.name: freeCodeCamp
resources.description: Nonprofit with a full, free coding curriculum and certifications in web development, data and programming, a free alternative to expensive bootcamps.

resources.name: Class Central
resources.description: Search engine and reviews for online courses from universities and platforms, with curated lists of courses that are still completely free and how to avoid paying for certificates you don't need.

resources.name: Student Borrower Protection Center
resources.description: Nonprofit focused on student debt, with research and resources on student loan servicers, predatory schools and borrower rights.

resources.name: Save the Student
resources.description: Independent UK site on student money: student finance, budgeting, banking and avoiding scams, with free tools and practical guides written for students.

resources.name: Center for Auto Safety
resources.description: Nonprofit car safety advocacy group with free guides on recalls, defects and lemon laws, including a state-by-state ranking of lemon law protections.

resources.name: CarComplaints.com
resources.description: Independent database of owner-reported car problems by make, model and year, showing the most common defects, repair costs and worst model years before you buy.

resources.name: Consumers for Auto Reliability and Safety (CARS)
resources.description: Nonprofit auto safety and consumer group with resources on unrepaired recalls in used cars, dealer practices and car buyers' rights.

resources.name: US PIRG
resources.description: Nonprofit consumer watchdog with free consumer tips, product safety alerts and campaigns on right to repair, hidden fees and dangerous products.

resources.name: ScamAdviser
resources.description: Free website checker that gives an automated trust score for online shops based on domain age, ownership, hosting and user reports. A quick first check before buying from an unfamiliar store.

resources.name: CHOICE
resources.description: Australia's leading independent consumer organisation. Product testing, buying guides and campaigns against misleading pricing and unfair business practices.

resources.name: Consumer Rights Wiki
resources.description: Community wiki that documents anti-consumer practices by companies and products: forced subscriptions, features removed after purchase, hidden fees and devices that stop working when servers shut down.

resources.name: Deceptive Patterns
resources.description: Long-running catalog of deceptive design tricks like hard-to-cancel subscriptions, sneaky add-ons and fake urgency, with real examples so you can recognize them before they cost you.

resources.name: Dark Patterns Tip Line
resources.description: Coalition project, backed by consumer and digital rights groups, where people report manipulative designs such as subscription traps and hidden charges. Reports are used for research and advocacy.

resources.name: JustDeleteMe
resources.description: Community-maintained directory of direct links to delete accounts on hundreds of websites and services, rated by how easy or hard each company makes it.

resources.name: Citizens Advice – Damaged, Lost or Delayed Parcels
resources.description: Step-by-step UK guide from the charity on who is responsible when a parcel is lost, damaged or late (usually the seller, not the courier) and how to get a refund or replacement.

resources.name: Which? – Delivery Rights
resources.description: Guidance from the UK consumer association on your rights when online orders arrive late, damaged or not at all, including template letters to claim from the retailer.

resources.name: 17TRACK
resources.description: Free universal package tracker covering thousands of carriers worldwide. Handy for international orders where tracking is handed between couriers, and for checking whether a 'delivery problem' text is genuine.

resources.name: EveryoneOn
resources.description: Nonprofit that helps low-income households find low-cost internet plans and affordable computers in their area, plus free digital skills training.

resources.name: NCLC – Utility Rights
resources.description: Resources from the National Consumer Law Center on utility shutoffs, payment plans and bill assistance programs, and what protections customers have when they fall behind.

resources.name: National Energy Action
resources.description: The UK's fuel poverty charity, with free advice on cutting energy bills, dealing with energy debt and accessing grants and support schemes.

resources.name: ACCAN
resources.description: Australia's peak body for phone and internet consumers. Free tip sheets on contracts, billing disputes, financial hardship and choosing a provider.

resources.name: Surveillance Self-Defense (EFF)
resources.description: Free guides from the Electronic Frontier Foundation on protecting your privacy online: strong passwords, two-factor authentication, secure messaging and avoiding tracking.

resources.name: Privacy Guides
resources.description: Independent, nonprofit, community-run site with privacy and security recommendations for browsers, email, messaging and more. Explains the trade-offs instead of selling products.

resources.name: Have I Been Pwned
resources.description: Free service to check whether your email address or phone number has appeared in a data breach, with optional alerts for future breaches.

resources.name: Big Ass Data Broker Opt-Out List
resources.description: Community-maintained list of data brokers and people-search sites with direct opt-out links and instructions, prioritized by which ones matter most.

resources.name: Privacy Rights Clearinghouse
resources.description: Nonprofit privacy organization with consumer guides and a searchable Data Breach Chronology to check which companies have exposed customer data.

resources.name: noyb – European Center for Digital Rights
resources.description: Nonprofit led by Max Schrems that enforces GDPR through strategic complaints against big tech. Useful explainers on your data rights in Europe, such as access and deletion requests.

resources.name: Open Rights Group
resources.description: UK digital rights organisation campaigning on privacy, data protection and online surveillance, with explainers on how changes in the law affect your data.
